findings.quote: I took dv over dx as acceleration
findings.note: This is the wrong method, not the right one: taking dv/dx as the acceleration is exactly common_mistakes[2], the option-4 slip, and the sidecar repeats the identical string as mistakes[2].route. A student who solved it correctly (multiplied dv/dx by v to get −2av³) sees only this phrase, taps it, and is diagnosed with the very error they avoided, while a student who really made that error cannot be separated from them at all.
findings.fix: I multiplied v by dv/dx to get acceleration

notes: The menu is broken in two directions at once: the right route describes a wrong method, and it is character-for-character the same as the only wrong route on the menu, so no tap can distinguish anybody. I filed it once, on right_route, because mistakes[2].route is correct for its own entry and should stay. The fix is the separating step: step 1 (dt/dx = 2ax + b) and the inversion are both shared by the option-4 student, so the earliest unshared move is multiplying dv/dx by v; checked as first person, 8 tokens, no two-digit number, and free of the machine-rejected wording. mistakes[0] distractor flag is honest - I confirmed that dropping the v-factor gives ±2av², swapping the coefficients gives ±2bv³, and nothing produces the mixed ab form. mistakes[1] typed calculation with a null route is right: the approach was correct and the coefficients and a sign went wrong. mistakes[2] concept is right - treating a distance-derivative as acceleration is a wrong belief, not a slip. Indices align.
